title: Introduce Interactive RAG Lab notebooks and compact API reference for tool-bindings
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: ship a low-friction, interactive learning surface for engineers who want to try Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) patterns against Redwood with real tool-binding manifests. This PR adds a set of Jupyter/Colab-compatible notebooks (lightweight, executable), a compact API reference for tool binding schemas, and a small sandbox integration so the docs site can launch an ephemeral playground connected to the guide.

What this changes (single continuous description): Adds a step-by-step RAG Lab walkthrough (authoring -> index -> agent -> tool binding -> eval) that runs locally in a devcontainer or in Colab, plus a compact reference page that documents the canonical fields for tool_binding manifests we expect in examples and quickstarts. The notebooks include seeded small-index examples and a mocked tool shim so readers can exercise tool-calls without provisioning external services. The site integration wires the new lab into the /quickstarts and adds a short tutorial card on the docs homepage.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add RAG Lab notebook templates (site/snippets/notebooks/rag-lab-01.ipynb, rag-lab-02.ipynb)
- [x] Add compact API reference for tool-binding schema (site/content/reference/tool-bindings-compact.md)
- [x] Add docs page with stepwise authoring guide and local-run instructions (site/content/quickstarts/rag-local-lab.md)
- [x] Devcontainer and docker-compose sandbox for reproducing examples locally (static/sandbox/devcontainer.json, sandbox/docker-compose.yml)
- [x] Add JSON schema and examples for tool manifests (site/data/tool-bindings/compact-schema.yaml)
- [x] Update site navigation and homepage quickstart tile
- [x] CI docs build passes, add smoke tests for notebook render pipeline

Compatibility notes: notebooks are intentionally small and pin model calls to the Redwood hosted sandbox endpoint; the examples include a toggle to switch between 'mock' and 'live' backends. The compact schema mirrors the runtime's tool-binding surface but intentionally omits advanced enterprise fields (auth integration, kms keys) to keep the quickstart approachable.

Related work: builds on work in ENG-1289 (tool-binding standardization) and references the RAG authoring patterns in the examples repo. Internal checklist item in PM-328 specified an interactive playground for Q4 content.

Links: Example notebook preview: https://deploy-preview/docs/rag-lab (internal preview), Tool-binding compact schema: site/data/tool-bindings/compact-schema.yaml

How to review: The notebooks are opinionated but self-contained. Reviewers should: run the devcontainer locally and confirm the notebooks execute end-to-end (mock mode), verify the compact schema covers the minimal fields required by runtime and that examples can be validated with the included schema validator, and scan the new docs copy for clarity and actionable steps.

release_notes: Added an interactive RAG Lab (notebooks + devcontainer) and a compact tool-binding API reference to help engineers prototype agent tool-calls locally. Includes sandbox devcontainer and an example JSON schema for tool manifests.
notes_for_release: This is documentation-only and examples-first; no runtime changes. Product teams may link to the lab from onboarding emails. Recommend adding the lab to the next docs newsletter and tracking uptake via the docs site internal analytics.
